sourceTitle: Anthony Mackie Says It’s ‘Hard’ to Date As an Older Man
sourceSummary: Anthony Mackie has apparently found it ‘hard’ to date as an ‘older man.’ Not only is he a fresh 48 years old, but has he ever heard of Leonardo DiCaprio? — Photo: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images Anthony Mackie is down in the dumps about dating. Last night, on Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen , the 48-year-old actor was asked if he was planning to get married again and had the gall to claim that he’s getting rejected because he’s too old. “You know, I’m an older man,” Mackie explained, “and I feel like being an older man, women don’t like older men.” “What? That is absolutely not true!” exclaimed host Andy Cohen, a man who is surely well-versed in age-gap relationships. “Older men with Marvel money?” asked Mackie’s fellow guest and man in his 40s, Jamie Dornan, in disbelief. “Yeah, right!” Cohen said. “Excuse me … older, jacked men who look like him?” Despite all this hyping, Mackie was not reassured. “It’s hard as an older man,” he insisted. “Women don’t like older men. They like younger, fruitful men.” This isn’t the first time Mackie has complained about his (relatively young) age interfering with his love life. In a 2025 interview with People , he said, “The idea of dating is really hard” mostly because he’s a cinematic superhero, but also because “I’m older, and I don’t do the apps.” Mackie was previously married to his childhood sweetheart, Sheletta Chapital

sourceTitle: ‘If He Knew How Much Stuff I Was Buying, He’d See Me Differently’
sourceSummary: In this week’s ‘My Two Cents,’ The Cut’s personal-finance columnist, Charlotte Cowles, speaks with couples in conflict over each other’s online shopping. — Photo-Illustration: by The Cut; Photos: Getty Images It’s widely known that money is a leading cause of marital conflict. But what about online-shopping habits? “ Stealth shopping ” — when couples hide purchases from each other or hope the other won’t notice when a package shows up — has been on the rise for years (along with problematic online shopping more generally). Sure, plenty of partners choose to keep their finances separate and spend their money how they see fit. But there’s a difference between independence and deception: When you’re squirreling away packages to keep your significant other from noticing, things can get weird. Below, three women share the online-shopping conflicts that have nearly upended their own relationships. My husband and I keep our money in three pots — his, mine, and ours — and we don’t ask each other about our separate expenses. I think it’s healthy, and it works for us for the most part. He can spend his money on golf or whatever, and I spend my money on Botox and things he doesn’t need to know about. But sometimes my online shopping feels a little furtive.
